message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films that hit theaters (or streaming platforms) in 2020:

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern twist on the classic horror tale, it blends psychological suspense with social commentary on abuse and gaslighting. |
| 2 | **Uncut Gems** | Josh and Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett | Sandler delivers an intense, frenetic performance as a charismatic jeweler whose gambling addiction spirals out of control. |
| 3 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced dialogue and stylish visuals make this heist caper both witty and action‑packed. |
| 4 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen | Though more courtroom drama than traditional thriller, its tense pacing and sharp script keep viewers on edge. |
| 5 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Scorsese’s epic saga of organized crime spans decades; its use of de-aging tech and stellar ensemble cast add intrigue. |
| 6 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen | A Danish film that turns a simple premise into a chilling exploration of paranoia and mob mentality. |
| 7 | **The Night House** | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Lane | A psychological thriller that uses supernatural elements to probe grief, memory, and domestic secrets. |
| 8 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A Spanish allegory about class struggle that escalates into a brutal survival game—highly unsettling and thought‑provoking. |
| 9 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime‑drama that builds tension through a medieval duel framed as a legal investigation. |
|10 | **The Little Things** | John Lee Hancock | Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, Jared Leto | A noir‑style mystery where two detectives pursue a serial killer while their own personal demons threaten to derail the case. |

These ten films represent a mix of mainstream blockbusters, indie gems, and international releases—all praised for their storytelling, performances, or stylistic flair. If you’re looking for something specific—like a sub‑genre focus or a particular director—let me know and I can narrow it down further!
